content: Trolamine salicylate is an analgesic approved by the FDA for the treatment of musculoskeletal pain and osteoarthritis. Common side effects include erythema and skin irritation. For adults, it is indicated to temporarily relieve minor pain associated with arthritis, simple backache, muscle strains, sprains, and bruises. There is limited information regarding off-label uses, both guideline-supported and non-guideline-supported, in adult patients. For pediatric patients, there is limited information regarding FDA-labeled indications and off-label uses, whether guideline-supported or not. Contraindications for trolamine salicylate are not well-documented in the drug label. Warnings include that it is for external use only. Individuals prone to allergic reactions from aspirin or salicylates should consult a doctor before use. The product should be used only as directed, and users should avoid tight bandaging, using it with a heating pad, contact with eyes or mucous membranes, and application to wounds or damaged skin. Discontinue use and consult a doctor if the condition worsens, symptoms persist for more than seven days or recur, redness is present, or irritation develops. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should consult a healthcare professional before use. Keep the product out of reach of children, and if swallowed, seek medical help or contact a Poison Control Center immediately. There is limited information available regarding clinical trial experience, postmarketing experience, drug interactions, and monitoring of trolamine salicylate. For administration, adults and children over 12 years should apply the product generously to the affected area, massage it into the skin until thoroughly absorbed, and repeat as necessary, but not more than four times daily. There is no FDA guidance on the use of trolamine salicylate in specific populations, including pregnant women, nursing mothers, pediatric patients, geriatric patients, specific gender or racial populations, or those with renal or hepatic impairment. Additionally, there is no guidance for use in females of reproductive potential, males, or immunocompromised patients. The mechanism of action, structure, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology of trolamine salicylate are not well-documented in the drug label. Similarly, there is limited information regarding clinical studies, how the drug is supplied, and storage instructions. There is no established interaction between alcohol and trolamine salicylate. Patients should consult their doctor about the effects of consuming alcohol while using this medication.
